airport.name: Zadar Airport
airport.description: Zadar Airport sits in Zemunik Donji, about 30 km (36 min) by road from the villa. In summer 2026 it had 68 regular scheduled routes, 50 of them operated by Ryanair (Ryanair has a base here); in winter almost everything stops apart from domestic Croatia Airlines flights (Zagreb, Pula) and a twice-weekly Croatia Airlines link to Munich.

transfers.description: About 30 km and 35-40 minutes by car from the ZAD terminal to the villa, via Zadar's ring road and the Nin road. You avoid the Old Town entirely, and the villa has its own driveway parking.
Fixed-price airport transfer to Privlaka/Sabunike: about €55 for a standard car or €70 for a passenger van, per vehicle and not per person. A 20% surcharge applies between midnight and 06:00.
Online transfer marketplaces quote about €68–69 one way for a sedan (1–3 people) and about €100 for an 8-seat minivan.
Uber operates pickups at ZAD, and Bolt is also reported in Zadar. The official taxi rank is directly opposite the arrivals exit. Use the app's quote for Sabunike.

legs.leg: Airport shuttle ZAD → Gaženica ferry port → Zadar bus station → Old Town
Liburnija suburban line 101/102 Zadar bus station → Privlaka (a Sabunike stop is listed on some runs)

transfers.description: The budget route costs about €8.20 per person: the €5 airport shuttle to Zadar bus station, then the Liburnija suburban bus to Privlaka/Sabunike for €3.19. It works well on weekdays, but at weekends only three buses a day run to Privlaka.

Major rental brands have desks at or next to the ZAD terminal (Avis/Budget, Enterprise/National, Europcar/Goldcar, Hertz, Sixt, plus local firms). A car is worth having in Sabunike for trips to Nin, Pag, Zadar and Paklenica.

tolls.description: The A1 motorway (Zagreb–Split) is tolled by distance. A car (category I) pays €17.30 from Zagreb to Posedarje, or €17.60 to Zadar centar; the cheaper IA category applies to motorcycles.
Slovenian motorways need an e-vignette. It costs €16 for 7 days or €32 for 1 month for a car.
Austrian motorways need a vignette. In 2026 it costs €9.60 for 1 day or about €12.80 for 10 days. The Tauern and Karawanken tunnels have separate section tolls.

ferries.days: 26–28 Jun Fri/Sat/Sun; 3 Jul–30 Aug Mon/Wed/Fri/Sat/Sun; extension to 6 Sep Wed/Fri/Sat/Sun
ferries.description: In 2026 Jadrolinija ran a 4-hour fast catamaran between Ancona and Zadar's Gaženica port from late June to early September. It carries foot passengers only, no cars. From the port it is a 30-minute drive to the villa.
Guests bringing a car from Italy can take the overnight car ferry from Ancona to Split (about 9–11.5 h, run by Jadrolinija and SNAV), then drive about 2 h 15 min north on the A1 to Sabunike.

alternativeAirports.name: Split Saint Jerome Airport
alternativeAirports.description: Split Saint Jerome Airport: 139 km, about 2 h 01 min by car to the villa. Split is a larger airport than Zadar and widens the choice of routes and dates (its network was not researched here). The drive is all motorway on the A1.

alternativeAirports.name: Rijeka Airport
alternativeAirports.description: Rijeka Airport: 236 km, about 3 h 35 min by car to the villa. Rijeka airport is on Krk island, and the drive crosses the Krk bridge. Its route network was not researched.

alternativeAirports.name: Zagreb Franjo Tuđman International Airport
alternativeAirports.description: Zagreb Franjo Tuđman International Airport: 307 km, about 3 h 38 min by car to the villa. Zagreb is Croatia’s capital and main hub, and the best fallback in winter, when ZAD has almost no international flights. Guests can connect onward to ZAD on Croatia Airlines (up to 11 flights a week in summer 2026) or drive about 3.5 h on the A1.

alternativeAirports.name: Ljubljana Jože Pučnik Airport
alternativeAirports.description: Ljubljana Jože Pučnik Airport: 383 km, about 4 h 47 min by car to the villa. Ljubljana (Slovenia) is an option for Slovenian guests. Its route network was not researched.

alternativeAirports.name: Trieste Airport
alternativeAirports.description: Trieste Airport: 410 km, about 5 h 15 min by car to the villa. Trieste (Italy): the drive crosses Slovenia. Its route network was not researched.

alternativeAirports.name: Pula Airport
alternativeAirports.description: Pula Airport: 408 km, about 5 h 52 min by car to the villa. Pula is in Istria. Its drive time looks long, but it has a direct Croatia Airlines connection to ZAD.

alternativeAirports.name: Venice Marco Polo Airport
alternativeAirports.description: Venice Marco Polo Airport: 518 km, about 6 h 21 min by car to the villa. Venice Marco Polo is a large gateway, but at about 6.5 h it only makes sense for long stays or a combined road trip.

alternativeAirports.name: Treviso Airport
alternativeAirports.description: Treviso Airport: 518 km, about 6 h 30 min by car to the villa. Treviso is the secondary airport for Venice.

publicTransport.description: FlixBus connects Zadar bus station with Zagreb, Ljubljana, Graz, Vienna, Munich, Prague and Budapest, plus the whole Croatian coast and Plitvice. From the bus station, the villa is 20 km (28 min) by car, or a Liburnija suburban bus to Privlaka.
No passenger trains run to Zadar. Rail travellers ride HŽPP to Knin, then take a bus to Zadar (about 1 h 50 min). For most guests a direct coach from Zagreb is simpler.

Liburnija suburban buses run between Zadar bus station and Privlaka about 14 times on weekdays, but only 3 times on Saturdays, Sundays and holidays. The fare is €3.19. Nin, the nearest town, is 5 km and 9 minutes from the villa by car.
